SUMMARY

Full-stack engineer three years out of school, currently shipping payment and onboarding flows at a mid-stage fintech-adjacent SaaS. Comfortable owning a feature end-to-end — schema design, API, React UI, and the on-call rotation that follows. Started in internships writing Python services, spent two years at a Series-B consumer startup growing into a primary author of the React codebase, and now operate as the second engineer on a small platform team where the work has shifted toward reliability, data integrity, and reviewing other people's PRs.


EXPERIENCE

Software Engineer II — Plinth Financial
Onboarding Platform · Brooklyn, NY · 2025 – Present

One of three engineers on the team that owns customer onboarding, KYC, and the underwriting hand-off for a B2B payments product. Stack is TypeScript, Node (Fastify), Postgres, and a React + Remix front-end. On-call once every six weeks.

- Rebuilt the KYC verification flow from a 12-step linear form into a saved-state wizard with resumable sessions; cut median time-to-complete from 9m12s to 4m48s and reduced abandonment past step 3 by 31% over the 8-week measurement window.
- Owned the migration from Knex to Drizzle ORM across 47 query sites in the onboarding service. Wrote a codemod that handled 80% of the call-site rewrites, paired with two engineers on the remainder, and shipped behind a per-route flag with zero rollback events.
- Built the document-upload pipeline (S3 presigned URLs, virus scanning via ClamAV, async OCR through AWS Textract, structured field extraction). Now processes ~14k documents/week at a 99.7% success rate; prior vendor solution was costing $0.42/doc, this came in at $0.06/doc.
- Designed and shipped the audit-log service for compliance — append-only Postgres table with row-level hashing, structured event taxonomy, and a Retool dashboard for the compliance team. Replaced an ad-hoc CSV-export workflow that took the ops lead two days per quarter.
- Lead engineer on the React 18 → 19 upgrade across the onboarding app (~140 components). Coordinated with design on Suspense boundaries, untangled three legacy class components, and shipped without a customer-visible regression.

Software Engineer I — Tessera Labs
Consumer Products · Remote · 2023 – 2025

Series-B consumer marketplace (~70 employees when I joined, ~180 when I left). Wore many hats; ended up as one of two primary authors of the React/Next.js front-end and the GraphQL gateway behind it.

- Shipped the seller-onboarding redesign that moved sellers from a single 23-field form to a progressive 4-step flow with inline validation and Stripe Connect embedded onboarding. Conversion from "started" to "first listing live" went from 38% to 61% over the quarter following launch.
- Built the search-results page from scratch on top of Algolia — faceted filters, saved searches, infinite scroll with cursor pagination, and a server-rendered shell that improved Lighthouse performance score from 54 to 86.
- Migrated the GraphQL gateway from Apollo Server v3 to v4 and introduced persisted queries, cutting p95 query payload size by 62% and removing two recurring rate-limit incidents tied to mobile clients.
- Owned the move from Heroku Postgres to AWS RDS, including a zero-downtime cutover using logical replication. Wrote the runbook the team still uses for subsequent database migrations.
- Built the internal admin tool used by the trust-and-safety team for listing review and account actions. ~30 daily users; replaced four Retool boards plus a Google Sheet.

Software Engineering Intern — Halberd Analytics
Data Platform · Atlanta, GA · Summer 2022 & Summer 2023

Two consecutive summers on the data-platform team at a B2B analytics company. Wrote Python services and helped the platform team ship the v2 of their ingest API.

- Returning intern in summer 2023: built the schema-validation layer for incoming customer events using Pydantic + a custom diff-against-registered-schemas check; rolled out across 12 customer integrations.
- First-summer project: a Slack bot that surfaced data-quality alerts to the on-call channel from the existing Great Expectations runs; still in production at offer-return time.
